It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 2/23 (309), 4/3/1(402) and 19/19(4 16) total area 12 Bigha and 07 Biswas, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas,
Delhi (in short, the said land).
4. It is stated that the petitioners are entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioners as the physical possession of the land has not been taken and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioners.

The LAC passed the award in a mechanical way without applying the mind and without going through the claim filed by the petitioners, as such the award is not acceptable to the petitioners, and they have received the awarded amount under protest and without prejudice to their rights.
The LAC failed to take note of the actual and practical market value of the said land and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.
The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value adjudicated by the courts.
The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

5. It is stated that the said land is well connected with the transport, telecommunication, roads and have all the basic amenities in and around the surrounding areas i.e. Mundka railway station is 1.5 kms away from the said land, Mundka Udyog Vihar Extension is located at a distance of LAC no.

CRPF Training school and Tuda Mandi are around 6 & 5 kms away from the said land respectively;
Ganga International School is about 3 kms from the said land, Deen Bandhu Chhotu Ram Sr.
Secondary School and Polytechnic is about 2 kms from the said land, wellknown school namely Haryana Shakti Senior Secondary School, police Station Kanjawala and MCD hospital and dispensary are about 3 kms away from the said land, 220 KW substation and various banks are about 3 kms away from the said land.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
16. I have heard the Ld. Counsel for UOI.
None had appeared on behalf of petitioner and DDA to address the final arguments.
Petitioner and DDA even failed to file written submissions though opportunity was granted.
Therefore, this Court deems it fit to pass judgment on merits of the case.

My issue-wise findings and determination are as under : -
1.

Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
17.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr.
LAC no. 324/ 2016 (Award No. 16/0506/DC(NW)) Naresh Singh v. Union of India & Anr.
Page no. 8 of 11 v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".

20. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

22. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 23.

As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No.
19//19 (4-16), has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.

24. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:-
(1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
